{{Quote|Swoop jockeys have the brains of a blister gnat&mdash;and about the same life expectancy.|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels">''[[The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref>}}
A '''swoop''', also known as a '''swoop bike''', was a type of [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] vehicle with focus on speed, meneuverability and power.<ref name="secrets">''[[The Secrets of Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire]]''</ref> 

It was similar to a [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bike]], of which it was simply an overpowered version, and described as "an engine with a seat." Swoops were to speeder bikes what [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeders]] were to [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeders]]. Swoops were often used by gangs and criminals, and such organizations bore the mantle of [[Swoop gang/Legends|swoop gang]]. After the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] outlawed [[Podracing/Legends|podracing]], [[Swoop racing/Legends|swoop racing]] became the favored alternative. Swoop racing was popular on many planets, including [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], [[Manaan/Legends|Manaan]], [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]], [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], [[Telos IV|Telos]] (on [[Citadel Station]]), and [[Taris/Legends|Taris]]. There were, in fact, grand tournaments held on the Taris tracks before the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] bombardment. Some of the best-known swoop racers of their time were lost in the planet's destruction.<ref name="kotor1">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>

==Overview==
[[File:ThrillingEscape-EotEBtR.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A female Rodian and Human escape on a swoop bike]]
Swoops were capable of traveling at over six hundred kilometers per hour and [[Turbothruster/Legends|turbothrusters]] could also be used to improve their top speeds. While some could travel several hundred kilometers above a [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] surface, they generally kept a low altitude. Designed to be powerful, fast and maneuverable in the same time, they employed many flaps and control vanes to aid in controlling the unpredictable vehicles; still, they were not preferred by the common people.<ref name="secrets" /><ref name="tradingcards">{{Topps|set=1996 Topps Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire|cardname=Swoop|link=https://www.rebelscum.com/photo.asp?image=/sote/soteTC087.jpg}}</ref>

Prior to and during the [[Mandalorian Wars]] and [[Jedi Civil War]], some of the earliest swoop bikes could be found on [[Taris/Legends|Taris]]. Archaeologists theorize that [[Swoop racing/Legends|swoop racing]] originated on Taris, though given the near-total destruction of the planet's surface,<ref name="kotor1" /> this is difficult to prove. [[Lhosan Industries]], which conducted business on Taris during this time, was referred to as "the birthplace of the swoop bike." In any case, Taris was the hub of swoop racing during the time of the Jedi Civil War, and its destruction was a severe blow to the circuit. Nevertheless, swoop-bike racing survived on such planets as [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], [[Manaan/Legends|Manaan]], [[Telos IV]], [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]], and the moon [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]].

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] used the [[CK-6 swoop bike/Legends|CK-6 swoop bike]] in combat during the [[Battle of Orto Plutonia/Legends|Battle of Orto Plutonia]] and for transportation during the [[Battle of Khorm/Legends|Battle of Khorm]]. The [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]] also utilized swoops in the Clone Wars, deploying swoop-mounted [[IG lancer droid/Legends|IG lancer combat droids]] in the [[Battle of Muunilinst/Legends|Battle of Muunilinst]].<ref name="Star Wars: Clone Wars Chapter 4">{{CW|4}}</ref>

[[File:SwoopClass_negvv.jpg|thumb|180px|Swoop bike types]]

The planet [[Zonju V]] was once plagued by swoop [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]]. In [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]], when [[Jaden Korr]] went there to meet up with a spaceport worker, he had to be faster than the local mercenary gangsters to get to a safe outpost and get out alive.

Many racing swoop bikes had their brakes removed to reduce weight, thus making the swoop bike faster. They also had deflector shields to protect them against impact. However, due to high speeds, many riders were thrown off and killed upon crashing into an object. Swoops are not to be mistaken for [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bikes]].

Swoops were widely used to travel by land in the area of [[Bartyn's Landing]], on the planet [[Lamaredd/Legends|Lamaredd]], in the five centuries after its initial settlement. A prosperous local business was [[Ackrahbala's Swoops & Speeders]], and illegal swoop [[Cargo Track race]]s were regularly held.<ref name="BL">{{GamerCite|7|Bartyn's Landing (article)}}</ref> The police used swoops to travel through the coastline.<ref name="R">{{GamerCite|7|Reckonings}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Swoops appeared in the [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] for the extended CGI scenes of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]]. Concept art of the bikes, and their final appearance, featured two figures with long helmets, dubbed "coneheads". The concept art was used by the concurrently produced ''[[Shadows of the Empire]]'' multimedia project, although the riders were largely replaced by [[Gizz's Gang]].<ref name="secrets" /> The "conehead" figures still appear in the cover of [[Shadows of the Empire 3|''Shadows of the Empire'' 3]] and the [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (video game)|video game adaptation]].<ref name="Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire video game">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (video game)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' video game]]</ref>
